title: Synthetic hotspot reproducer and instrumentation plan
content:
Purpose:
This doc describes a deterministic synthetic workload + instrumentation plan to reproduce intermittent eviction cliffs and downstream NVMe paging events we see in prod traces. Goal is a compact, repeatable bench that exercises: sudden hotkey concentration, interleaved long/short sequence requests, and multi-tenant burst coupling that causes memory-bandwidth-driven eviction cascades.

Background / motivation:
- Multiple field incidents show short-lived tail-latency spikes correlated with a spike in page-fault IO and rapid resident-set shrinkage.
- Ad-hoc traces suggest the problem happens when a small hotset (1–5% of logical keys) receives >60% of active requests for ~5–30s while background batch churn and large-seqlen inference requests are present.
- Current unit benches don't produce the same NVMe / PCIe bandwidth contention patterns; we need a synthetic harness that reproduces the coupling between request mix, seqlen distribution, and KV residency.

Hypotheses to test:
1) Bandwidth saturation from mixed large-seqlen KV materialization + concurrent background spills triggers eviction waves that evict still-hot entries (false negatives), dropping reuse rate and causing repeat page-in bursts.
2) Burstiness alignment across tenants (two or more tenants peaking overlapping in time) multiplies effective hotset working set beyond residency headroom causing oscillation.
3) Small adjustments to prefetch aggressiveness and write-back batching can reduce amplitude of eviction cascades without increasing average latency.

Success criteria:
- Reproduce a clear eviction cascade: a precipitous drop in global reuse-rate (>=30% relative drop) accompanied by an NVMe IO throughput spike and increase in 95/99 latency within a 10–60s window.
- Reproducer run should be deterministic within 10% variation across repeated runs on the same infra config.

Synthetic workload design (reproducer):
1) Key-space and hotset:
   - total_keys: 10M logical keys (simulate footprint via KV IDs; actual resident entries depend on seqlen/activation).
   - hotset_ratio: variable [0.01, 0.05, 0.10] (1%/5%/10% of total_keys).
   - hot_access_skew: Zipfian alpha variable [0.7, 1.1] for hotset; background uniform for cold keys.
2) Request mix:
   - short requests: seqlen 8–64 tokens, 70% of RPS normally, primarily hit hotset.
   - long requests: seqlen 512–2048 tokens, 10–20% of RPS, random keys that cause large KV materialization and writebacks.
   - background churn: periodic large batch evictions (simulated by synthetic writes) that create writeback IO.
3) Burst model:
   - tenant_count: 3 simulated tenants sharing KV space.
   - burst_profile: exponential ramp to peak over 2–5s, hold 5–30s, then decay over 3–10s.
   - alignment parameter: skewed timing to create overlapping peaks for 2 tenants (controlled toggle).
4) Concurrency and batching:
   - control request concurrency to match production average RT and peak concurrency; include options to force synchronous vs async prefetch edges.

Instrumentation plan (what to collect):
- Serving runtime telemetry (per-request): request id, tenant id, key id, op type (read/write), seqlen, cache_hit boolean, latency ms, kv-prefetch events.
- Aggregates: reuse_rate (sampled window 1s), eviction_count, resident_entries, persistent_pageins/sec, NVMe throughput (MB/s), PCIe link utilization (if available), GPU memory occupancy, host DRAM bandwidth counters.
- Kernel / device level: iostat -x, blktrace, perf counters for memory bandwidth (uncore/pmu), nvme-cli telemetry, ftrace for page_fault events.
- Traces: pprof/flamegraphs from worker processes during window, and end-to-end request traces for top-K slowest requests.

Bench harness implementation notes:
- Implement harness in Python with a small C extension to generate high precision timing and request bursts; or reuse existing trace-replayer with new synthetic trace generator module.
- Provide deterministic RNG seed and record seed with run artifacts.
- Export harness knobs via a YAML scenario file: hotset_ratio, zipf_alpha, long_request_pct, alignment, burst_window.

Experiment matrix (initial):
- Vary hotset_ratio: 1%, 5%, 10%
- Vary long_request_pct: 10%, 20%, 30%
- Alignment: aligned peaks vs staggered peaks
- Prefetch aggressiveness: off / conservative / aggressive
- Background writeback batch size: small/medium/large (tunable)
Each cell: 3 runs, collect full telemetry, compare reuse-rate drop, nvme throughput spike amplitude, and tail latency shift.

Analysis plan:
- Post-process: align time-series by peak-start time, compute delta from baseline window preceding burst, and produce waterfall charts: reuse_rate vs resident_entries vs nvme_mb/s vs 95/99 latency.
- Compute cross-correlation between NVMe throughput and reuse_rate with varying lags to estimate causal lag.
- Produce per-tenant contribution breakdown to identify amplification from multi-tenant overlap.

Immediate next steps / ownerable tasks:
- Marcus: prototype synthetic generator module and scenario YAML (ETA 4 days).
- Sofia: add perf counter / iostat ingestion pipeline to bench infra (ETA 6 days).
- Evan: instrument runtime tiny opt-in tracepoint to tag prefetch and eviction decisions (ETA 5 days).
- Aisha: run initial experiment matrix on staging nodes and capture artifacts (ETA 7 days).

Artifacts to land with ticket:
- harness repo branch + scenario configs
- raw telemetry tarball (time-series + perf)
- analysis notebook with aligned plots and cross-correlation output
- suggested runtime config tweaks to test (prefetch throttle, writeback coalescing window adjustments)

Open questions / risks:
- We may not be able to reproduce exact PCIe-level saturation without matching production hardware topology (NVLink/PCIe lanes). If so, focus on qualitative reproducibility and sensitivity curves.
- Sampling overhead: per-request tracing at production RPS will add noise; will use sampling + targeted full-trace windows.

Notes:
- Keep scenario files short and human-readable; prefer explicit seeds for reproducibility.
- Record kernel version and infra SKU in run metadata.

If this plan looks good I will open the harness branch and link it to KV-1234.
